# How this deck works {.hero #s00-how-to-use}

::: {.section-badge}
BMAN10750 · nine seminars, one idea each
:::

Every seminar gets an intuition and a simulation.

::: {.lede}
The worksheets already show you *how* to compute. These slides are about *why* the computation behaves the way it does — and every claim on them is one you can check yourself, live, in the browser.
:::

## The R runs here, in this page {#s00-webr}

::: {.slide-kicker}
No install · no account · nothing to download
:::

::: {.lede-min}
The grey boxes below are real R. Press **Run** and the code executes inside your browser — there is no server, and nothing you type is sent anywhere.
:::

::: {.sim-card .sim-text}
```{webr-r}
# Edit anything here, then press Run.
x <- rnorm(10, mean = 100, sd = 15)
round(mean(x), 2)
```
:::

::: {.try-this}
Press **Run** four or five times without changing a thing. The mean moves every time — *that* is the whole subject in one line.
:::

::: {.slide-footer}
First run takes a few seconds while R loads. After that it is instant.
:::
